visualReview.notes: Inspected 11 current portable views, including the retained 1024×640 summary. The square podium, stepped main hall, large pink dome, eight small domed pavilions, pointed perimeter arcades with open lower passages and upper coarse lattice, dark opaque hall/drum fields, pale eaves, bronze finials and separate tiered minaret are present. Original coarse cream diamond/grid geometry suggests decoration without copying historic motifs or inscriptions. Small pavilion decoration is deliberately sparse. Fine arabesques, calligraphy, interiors, furnishings, planting and adjacent causeway structures are excluded.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected 11 current shared-material/geographic-flat views, including the placement overlay. Six existing 256² graphs supply sandstone, raw limestone, ceramic tile, marble, painted metal and cast bronze. Seven merged roles include local opaque glazing; metric UVs and linear tints, with no embedded images or unique atlas. Each graph is read once and eviction disposes model geometry. Two masks replace the complete podium and mapped minaret base; all eight neighboring buildings remain host content. The flat overlay checks pose and replacement only. The standard DEM varies substantially at the shoreline and does not establish accurate water contact.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 27 current medium-fi views: Economy/High, noon/late light, street/block/skyline, silhouette, six details, four matched LODs and four transitions. The pink dome group, stepped hall, podium and tall detached minaret remain recognizable. Skyline retains three coarse open pointed bays per side, all eight pavilion silhouettes, simple finials and the exact minaret base. District adds coarse lattice, opaque facade fields and reduced drum windows. Street restores seven bays per side, main dome diamonds, drum eaves and further curve segments; closeup restores smaller dome diamonds and finer facets. Skyline omits inward arcade faces and thin underside details. Detail cameras can crop the minaret tip; whole views retain it. Context buildings are synthetic. Physical laptop/phone/tablet and full-city performance remains unmeasured.

fidelityReview.notes: Individual Putra Mosque: mapped square waterfront podium and separate minaret base,pink pointed arcade facades and upper abstract lattice fields,stepped pale main hall,windowed drum,large pink dome with original coarse cream diamond rhythm,eight smaller domed pavilions,bronze finials and tall tiered minaret. Historic arabesque artwork,calligraphy,furnished interiors,adjacent causeway/circulation buildings,landscaping and water surface are excluded. All original selected height/min_height tags are retained verbatim. The 25 m hall,33 m drum,63 m main shell,29/35/40 m inner pavilion stages,19/25/30 m outer stages and100 m minaret control the visualization nominally. The dome receives an estimated4 m finial. The separate65 m ring part,84 m center pole and60/35 m tower parts have unresolved component/datum semantics;their values are preserved without forcing incompatible geometry. Tier positions,spire profiles,arcades,eaves and precise stage dimensions are estimates,not surveyed measurements. Identity, retained envelopes, current part footprints and an undirected axis support approximate placement. Photograph-facing assignment, arcade counts, internal floor levels, lattice/diamond patterns, dome profiles, tower tiers and exact height datum semantics are estimates. The two 2006 pictures guide vocabulary, not complete current condition. Main shell63 m, estimated finial67 m and minaret100 m are nominal visualization levels, not survey verification. Unresolved65/84 m parts remain preserved in source without forcing incompatible geometry. Exact waterfront levels, stairs, thresholds, engineering, interiors and fine artwork remain unverified or omitted.
